papers.what_it_is: A numerical-simulation study that maps protein-ligand docking to a maximum vertex weight clique problem and solves it with QAOA and a multi-angle digitized-counterdiabatic QAOA (DC-QAOA) on 6, 8 and 12 qubits.

papers.what_it_is: A numerical-simulation study that introduces quantum active learning (QAL), pairing uncertainty-sampling strategies with equivariant quantum neural networks, and benchmarks it on a 2-qubit donut classification problem (positive result) and a 9-qubit tic-tac-toe problem (negative result).

existing.note: The abstract claim holds only for the slicing-a-donut problem with the equivariant EQNN-Z model. The main text gives 95% test accuracy after 6 queried labels (one example) against a full-label mean of 91.63 +/- 4.24%, and the gain over random sampling is only about one standard deviation. papers.what_it_is: A PhD thesis on classical reservoir computing (agricultural price forecasting, solving the Schrodinger equation with multi-step reservoir computing) and on quantum reservoir computing (circuit-family design by majorization, noise effects, time-series forecasting and a hybrid quantum-classical CNN for binding affinity), all in simulation.

It holds when both the number of gates and the error probability are small enough (p of about 0.0005 or below), the fidelity threshold 0.96 is empirical from four rows of Table 5.1 (the p = 0.0010 row has fidelity 0.956, below 0.96, yet the noisy reservoir still wins), and it is shown for one task (first excited energy of LiH, simulated noise channels, 100 runs per setting). existing.value: The author reports, from simulations of the first excited energy of LiH, that quantum reservoirs with amplitude damping noise outperform noiseless ones when the number of gates and the error probability are small enough (fidelity of the noisy final state above about 0.96, p of about 0.0005 or below), while the depolarizing and phase damping channels always worsen performance, even for small error probabilities.

These results imply that when the fidelity is greater than 0.96, the noisy reservoirs outperform the noiseless ones at QML tasks

Remarkably, the results show that for error rates p ≲ 0.0005 or state fidelities of at least 0.96, the presence of an amplitude damping channel renders better performance than noiseless reservoirs for QML tasks.
In the former cases, the performance of the noisy reservoirs is always worse than that of the noiseless one, even for small error probabilities.
